title: Celestis prototype - TTFT credits and privacy breakdown
summary: High-level discovery covering Celestis's prototype goals, time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations, free credits play for PLG onboarding, and privacy/compliance constraints for a potential dedicated or VPC/private deployment. Agreement to run an initial 1k-token throughput benchmark and to share security artifacts; Redwood to provision trial org with credits and follow up on pricing for dedicated pools.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim, Priya Nair (Redwood); Maya Ortiz, Liam Chen, Sara Gold (Celestis)

[00:00] Jared Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got about 45 ish minutes, is that still good?
[00:06] Maya Ortiz: Yep, perfect. We have 3 on our side, so quick intros — Maya platform, Liam ML eng, Sara security.
[00:14] Jared Kim: Awesome. Quick context, Redwood offers hosted API for fastest TTFT, Dedicated reserved pools for throughput and predictability, and Private/VPC for data residency. We'll focus on what helps your prototype move fastest but also meets your privacy bar.
[00:30] Liam Chen: Great. Our goal is to have a prototype that integrates with our backend within two weeks. TTFT is a huge deal — we want a demoable endpoint where product can hit first token within single-digit seconds. We're also evaluating if we should start hosted and then move to a VPC.
[00:46] Priya Nair: Totally — typical path is PLG via hosted with free credits for devs, get to first calls, then decide on Dedicated or Private depending on latency and data residency. How stringent is your data residency requirement?
[00:58] Sara Gold: We need EU residency for PII in user uploads, and keys must be customer-managed; we'll need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. SOC2 is a minimum.
[01:12] Jared Kim: Understood. We have SOC 2 and ISO attestation, and for Private deployments we do KMS integrations and full audit logs. For the hosted play, we can segregate logs and offer short retention for trial, but production EU residency generally pushes toward private or dedicated in-region.
[01:34] Maya Ortiz: Ok — in terms of quickstart, how much effort to get a prototype up and what's included in the free credits?
[01:41] Priya Nair: We typically create a trial org, allocate credits (we suggested 2k-5k tokens per dev depending on workload), and provide a starter prompt template and SDK snippets. Most teams hit first token in under an hour if they're using the SDK and have API keys. Real TTFT to demo-quality depends on model and sequence length — 1-2s for small contexts on hosted, 2-6s for larger contexts or bigger models.
[02:05] Liam Chen: That sounds promising. For throughput, our prototype will do batched summarization of documents ~3k tokens each, maybe 5 concurrent users. Any recommendations?
[02:16] Priya Nair: For 3k-token inputs, we recommend using model variants optimized for long context and enabling streaming. Also caching prefix prompts and setting batch size—dedicated pools make heavy batching/troughput more predictable. If you're prototyping, start hosted to validate quality, then move to Dedicated reserved GPU for predictable p99 latency once you lock shape of traffic.
[02:39] Sara Gold: Can we get a sense of economics? Our compliance team will want to compare hosted per-token costs vs dedicated monthly commits.
[02:46] Jared Kim: We'll share a pricing sheet — hosted is usage-based so good for prototyping; Dedicated has commit tiers with lower unit cost and SLOs. We'll include a model-selection and quantization suggestion to cut unit cost.
[03:00] Maya Ortiz: Liam — are you able to run Redwood SDK later this week?
[03:04] Liam Chen: Yes, I can. Does Redwood provide sample payloads for the 3k-token case?
[03:08] Priya Nair: We'll drop a sample repo and a small script to run a 1k/3k token throughput test. Also include a small harness to measure p50/p95/p99.
[03:20] Jared Kim: Quick question, any internal procurement stalls we should know about? timelines, reviewers?
[03:25] Maya Ortiz: We're small but Security is very involved — Sara will sign off. Timeline: prototype this month, decision on hosting approach next month.
[03:33] Sara Gold: We need to see KMS support, sidecar network controls for private, and evidence of audit logging and SSO/SAML integration. Also want to confirm we can disable retention for hosted trial if we need.
[03:48] Priya Nair: Yes, we can set shorter retention and an opt-in for audit logs. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC integrations for enterprise orgs.
[03:57] Jared Kim: Let's outline next steps so nothing falls through. We'll: 1) provision a trial org with 2000 free credits, 2) share SOC2 + security whitepaper and KMS docs, 3) Priya runs a 1k-token throughput run with your sample model, 4) schedule benchmark follow-up next week.
[04:18] Liam Chen: Sounds good. On the dedicated side, how long to spin up a reserved pool if we went that route?
[04:25] Priya Nair: For Enterprise customers, dedicated capacity can be commissioned in a few days to a couple of weeks depending on region and commit. For pilots we sometimes use burst capacity or shared dedicated to start faster.
[04:40] Maya Ortiz: Are there any gotchas when moving from hosted to private?
[04:44] Jared Kim: The main items are network connectivity (VPC peering, private link), customer-managed keys and audit ingestion. Model variant compatibility is usually seamless, but we'll run a staging passthrough to test rollouts and KV cache behavior.
[04:59] Sara Gold: And what about on-prem possibilities? We have a customer with air-gapped requirements later but not for the prototype.
[05:05] Priya Nair: We offer on-prem for regulated customers; it requires a longer lead time and an ops runbook. For now, VPC/private cloud should be the right tradeoff.
[05:17] Jared Kim: Ok, quick recaps and responsibilities — I'll send pricing and security docs; Priya will run the benchmark and drop the sample harness; we'll set up your trial org and allocate credits.
[05:27] Maya Ortiz: Thanks. One more question: any known competitors offering easier TTFT? We looked at couple but wanted Redwood's differentiators.
[05:34] Jared Kim: Many vendors claim low TTFT but Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and the routing/rollback patterns — plus first-class dev experience and observability. We'll include a short note on our differences.
[05:46] Liam Chen: Ok great. Let's set the follow-up for next Wednesday 16:00 UTC if that works.
[05:51] Sara Gold: Works for me.
[05:53] Jared Kim: Awesome, we'll send calendar invite. Thanks everyone, talk soon.
next_steps: Provision trial org and allocate 2000 credits
Send SOC2/ISO + security whitepaper and KMS integration docs
Drop sample repo and 1k/3k token benchmarking harness
action_items: Priya Nair: run 1k-token throughput benchmark using Celestis sample by 2028-03-10
Jared Kim: send pricing sheet and security artifacts by 2028-03-05
Liam Chen: integrate SDK sample and send sample payloads by 2028-03-06
